title: October 19: SihtiBrain consolidated gradient-return and operator-memory controls
summary: Originally five closely related repository cards (plus two Qwen side projects), now consolidated into one surviving SihtiBrain repository. A hidden cable gradient may become observable on return through a state-dependent operator. V2's state-dependent and post-reset echoes survive, V3's adapted-vs-preset distinction and moving tracker fail their added-value controls, and memory/Qwen tests remain separately labelled archived negative or mixed results. Original protocols, code, figures and tests are kept under SihtiBrain/studies/. The repo consolidation is organizational; the source experiments are not newly verified by Genealogy.

nodes.claim: One consolidated gradient-and-ping laboratory: a limited soma misses dendritic state; state-dependent probe echoes and slow conductance changes can expose hidden distinctions in constructed circuits. V2/V3 and independent memory and Qwen side studies are preserved under studies/.
nodes.survived: Passive soma traces are identical for matched distributed inputs even when local cable modes differ. A state-dependent return echo in V2 separates such inputs (−0.11495), with an after-reset conductance echo (−0.04817). V3 complementary probes distinguish hidden states in a controlled toy. Source and tests now live in the SihtiBrain main repository.
nodes.killed: Fixed linear pulses are blind. V2 calcium-ratio learning did not beat the simpler three-factor baseline (62.13% versus 62.21% balanced accuracy), and V3 phase-blind tracking lost to velocity extrapolation (0.615 versus 0.781). AIBrain association memory lost to equal-size Hebbian storage (71.9% versus 95.4% at load 32); AIbrainV2 normalization explained most graph gain (53.4% versus 55.6%), while compact indexed storage scored 73.9%. Transformer activation injection did not restore the intended Qwen fact (2/12). No automatic segmentation or novel credit advantage has been established.
nodes.era: October 19: hidden state and queryable operators

edges.why: Translates the Sihti purification/residue intuition into a distributed cable observability question; no direct code inheritance or lossless residue reconstruction is claimed.
Both ask whether operator/graph rewrites preserve unrelated information, with substantially different synthetic writers, matrices and baseline controls.
A perturbation response depends on the cable operator and observation port; this is a concrete toy example of question/reader-relative response geometry, not proof of a universal spectrum.

motifs.title: Hidden local distinctions need an appropriate observer, not merely another pulse
motifs.description: SihtiBrain's symmetric soma is blind to branch modes; V2 changes operator visibility; V3 tests complementary temporal probes and reveals when phase averaging cancels the very direction used to distinguish states. A fixed linear cable does not magically recover local input detail through a second identical somatic pulse.

motifs.title: A measured feedback route is not an algorithmic credit-assignment advantage
motifs.description: Original SihtiBrain tests calcium read noise, tuft attenuation, ternary and live burst events; V2 isolates a teacher-driven apical path but its preregistered calcium-ratio algorithm fails against simpler three-factor controls. Distinguish possible pathways from superior learning and count externally supplied teaching information.

motifs.title: Memory in response geometry faces ordinary storage, normalization and interference baselines
motifs.description: AIBrain stores associations in a local matrix but loses to matched-size fast weights and suffers rewrite interference. AIbrainV2's fixed-W Schur-response read beats raw matrix multiplication but most of the gain is degree normalization, and compact indexed addressing wins at random keys. This connects conceptually to GraphNN without transferring its empirical conclusions.
